welcome.reasoning: A wins on draughtsmanship and internal coherence; B wins on nothing but ambition. ILLUSTRATION: A commits to a single light source from the upper left — the white volumes carry cool blue shadow planes on their right faces, the dome gradates around its curve, the terrace risers cast short shadows, and the stair flight actually descends into a landing that touches the hill. The cypress overlaps the wall and pins the cluster to the ground. Value in the hillside modulates with the landform, so the green mass reads as terrain rather than fill. B's hill is a fan of alternating light/dark stripes radiating from the bottom edge that bears no relation to any light source or to the topography — decorative barcode, not description of form. Its buildings are near-flat cream with arbitrary thin drop shadows that point different directions from cube to cube, and the lowest white box at mid-left floats with a flat base against a steep slope, no terrace, no contact shadow. The long stair flight simply stops in mid-air at its lower end. Worse, the entire top-right cluster is amputated by the phone's right edge mid-volume, which reads as overflow rather than a crop decision. COMPOSITION: B's corner-to-corner diagonal is the bolder gesture, and I wanted to reward it, but it drives the eye out through the top-right corner into the truncated buildings, and the mass it creates leaves the button sitting on a noisy striped field. A's low diagonal sets a horizon, lets the type breathe, and points back toward the CTA. TYPE: A holds one axis — logo, tagline and button all centred — with a generous, deliberate interval between wordmark and tagline. B aligns type and button flush left competently, but crams the tagline hard under the wordmark, killing the pause that makes a lockup read as a lockup, and it enlarges the wordmark to the point that it competes with the illustration for the same emphasis. A's real fault, and it is a real one, is the dead acreage in the middle third: nothing occupies the mid-left, and the illustration is small enough to read as an afterthought vignette rather than a stage. It survives that because everything it does draw, it draws correctly.
welcome.sharpnessNote: A is visibly the softer raster — pervasive film grain, fuzzier glyph edges, slightly muddy hill silhouette; B is crisp, clean-edged vector-like output. I registered this and excluded it from the judgement entirely. Note that the grain in A is not purely a resolution artefact: it is applied evenly as a paper texture across the blue field, which is a deliberate finish, whereas B's flat field is untextured. Even discounting sharpness completely, the decisions above stand.

goal.reasoning:
A wins on draughtsmanship and compositional depth; B wins only on information layer, and not by enough.

ILLUSTRATION — the decisive gap. A's temple is a coherent three-quarter view: the entablature and stylobate converge, the side colonnade's intercolumniations compress as they recede, a real ridge runs back from the pediment apex, and the whole thing sits on a plinth with a dark base line that pins it to the rock. Light comes hard from the left and stays there — lit front face, shadowed right flank, and the cliff below repeats the same logic with directional highlight streaks that actually describe convex folds and a recessed gully. The stipple is doing work: it grades across the cliff face to model form, and thins toward the lit ridge. Three depth planes (far hill, mid cliff, foreground sea) with a beach sliver where land meets water.

B's temple is two incompatible projections welded together: a flat orthographic elevation on the front (columns identical width, no convergence, isosceles pediment) glued to a parallel-oblique side whose columns show zero diminution over eight bays. Nothing shares a vanishing point. The light logic is inverted — the sky-facing roof plane is rendered the single darkest value in the building while the receding side wall reads nearly as bright as the sun-struck front, so the planes never separate. There is no cast shadow and no ground contact at all: the stylobate hovers on a cream sliver above the hill crest. The hill itself is a featureless dome with an unmistakable hard-edged rectangle of darker green cut into it and a straight diagonal band, neither of which follows the form — that is masking residue, not shading. The cypress is a flat lozenge with no trunk and no shadow. Add a soft orange bloom haloing the CTA into the green, a white/blue fringe along the entire coastline seam, and an orphaned navy bar floating on the grass at the bottom edge.

TYPE AND HIERARCHY. A pairs "GOAL" tightly to the title so the eyebrow reads as belonging to it, then opens a large gap to the figure — clear grouping. It also varies weight: a high-contrast, lighter-weight numeral against the heavier title, so name and number are distinguishable at a glance. B letterspaces the eyebrow wide and drops it a full line away, so it floats between the nav bar and the title with ambiguous ownership, and its gaps are near-uniform (eyebrow→title ≈ title→amount), which flattens the grouping. B's title and figure are both heavy blue at similar weight — a monotone slab where A has modulation.

WHERE B IS BETTER, honestly. B's progress track is a legible mint against the cream; A's unfilled track is a near-invisible hairline that makes the 62% hard to read as a ratio — a real defect. And B adds "₹25,000 a month • target September 2024," which answers the question the screen actually poses. That is the better product decision and A should steal it. But an extra metadata line and a visible track do not offset a building drawn in two projections at once with inverted light and no ground contact, plus visible compositing artefacts in three separate places.

COMPOSITION. A's rising left-to-right diagonal puts the temple small and distant at the upper right — the destination still far off, which is exactly right for a 62% goal — and leaves generous cream above. B enlarges the temple to hero scale on a symmetrical dome, which is bolder but reduces the scene to two flat planes and forfeits both the depth and the narrative.
goal.sharpnessNote: B is the visibly cleaner raster — crisper vector-hard edges, tighter anti-aliasing, no paper grain. A is noticeably softer throughout, with an allover print-grain texture and slightly fuzzy type edges, and it carries a faint horizontal seam across the green mid-cliff. I have set all of that aside; none of it entered the verdict. Note that A's grain is not only a raster property — it is also used compositionally as tonal modelling on the cliff, and that use I did judge. Conversely, B's hard-edged rectangle in the green, the CTA bloom, the coastline fringe and the orphaned navy bar are compositing errors, not resolution artefacts, and they counted against it.
